newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - High-octane mogas bid up.
newsitem.headline: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - High-octane mogas bid up.

text.p: High octane gasoline prices firmed on Thursday as a major continued to bid up the market, traders said.
The European major raised its bid for 50,000-barrels of 97-octane unleaded gasoline to $25.00 per barrel from $24.30 on Wednesday.
But despite the hike, no sellers surfaced.
The major said the requirement was for its own system.
"The high octane is very bullish.. it is very tight," it said.
Scarce supplies of octane enhancer MTBE in August were partially behind the rush for high-octane supplies, traders said.
A cut in reforming ouput and emerging regional demand for the grade were also major factors.
Meanwhile in the lower grades, Vietnam was heard to have bought three 50,000-barrel 92-octane August lifting cargoes at $1.00 per barrel over Singapore naphtha quotes, on a free-on-board China basis.
Naphtha edged up slightly with August swaps up 10 cents per barrel to $21.50/$21.60. A small backwardation re-emerged with September quoted at $21.40/$21.60.
But traders were still bearish amid weak north Asian demand.
"Middle distillate stocks in Japan and South Korea are very high and refiners are producing more light distillates," a South Korean refiner said. "Supply is greater than requirements."

Taiwan's state-owned Chinese Petroleum Corp (CPC) CHIP.CN has awarded its tender to buy 30,000 tonnes of September full-range naphtha to South Korean refiner Yukong Ltd at $203 per tonne on a cost-and-freight (c-and-f)
basis, industry sources said.
The cargo for delivery to Kaohsiung during September 1-30 is CPC's second full-range naphtha purchase this year.
It last bought an April 1-20 delivery cargo at $224 c+f from Swiss trader Glencore, traders said.

The official said the next tender for a full-range cargo would be for a November cargo and that CPC was considering issuing a tender on Friday for its heavy or naphthenic-and-aromatic (N+A) requirements for September.
Yukong has a term contract from January to December to supply CPC with 150,000 tonnes-per-year of N+A at around $3.75 per barrel over Singapore spot naphtha quotes, c-and-f, sources said.
